sources.title: GTA 6 Fan Says Rockstar Sent Them a Poster Just Because They Asked Nicely
sources.text: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through. Reddit user aogustoo shared their story in a post late last month. What began as a "shot-in-the-dark email" they sent to Rockstar asking for a signed GTA 6 poster has turned into what seems to be a heartwarming moment for them and the community. "A while ago I took a complete shot in the dark and emailed Rockstar," they said. "I shared how hyped I was for GTA VI and asked if there was any chance I could get a poster for my room. "Honestly, I expected an automated reply or nothing at all. To my absolute surprise, an executive actually answered and shipped an official GTA VI poster straight from their New York office to my home in Brazil." You can see images, which show not only the poster but the emails they supposedly sent to receive it, above. As Rockstar (and the rest of the world) count down the days to GTA 6's November 19 launch, fans will no doubt be on the lookout for official merchandise like this. As many have pointed out, it's unclear if Rockstar truly took the time to send the poster, but the community is still looking to the moment as something worth celebrating as the countdown continues. "This is a massive W tho," Rockstar content creator @videotech said on X/Twitter . "This guy isn’t an influencer or someone famous, literally just a random Rockstar fan. Very kind of Rockstar and Take-Two to take the time and effort to do this." "​I blurred out all personal addresses, names, and contact emails to respect their privacy," aogustoo added. "Please don't flood their inbox with requests, as I'm pretty sure this was just a rare act of kindness from someone on their team." There's still so much about GTA 6 that we don’t know, but one thing is for sure: Rockstar will probably get even more emails after this. While we wait to learn more about the next Grand Theft Auto game ahead of its November 19 launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, you can check out IGN's recent interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson . You can also read about what Nintendo had to say about the chances of seeing GTA 6 on Switch 2 , some recently revealed radio stations , and even a batch of new screenshots . sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: DMZ — 5 Features to Get Excited for in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s New Mode
sources.text: Call of Duty’s upcoming DMZ mode sounds like it’s shaping up to be something special. Set on the new Hajin map and inspired by the events and locations from Modern Warfare 4 ’s Campaign, this open-world combat environment will challenge you to loot, complete objectives, fight both enemies and rival Operators, and extract before everything you’ve earned is lost. Recent intel drops on the official Call of Duty Blog have given us a much clearer picture of what awaits in Hajin when DMZ launches as part of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Players who have digitally pre-ordered or pre-purchased Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 can gain Early Access to the game’s Campaign starting Friday, October 16 and all of DMZ starting Tuesday, October 20. The events within DMZ are set after the main MW4 Campaign, leaving a power vacuum in its wake. Now it’s up to you to identify a new, mysterious threat and dismantle its operations across the DMZ through various deployments. From scavenging for crafting materials and experimenting with new technology, to leveling up an Operator, the mode sounds like it offers plenty to look forward to. Here are five features to get excited for when you begin your deployment. The 3D Printer will be available back at the Forward Operating Base (FOB) between deployments and will serve as your primary crafting station to build equipment and upgrades for your loadout before you drop into Hajin. The Call of Duty Blog shares that , as you progress through the DMZ, you’ll unlock new crafting recipes to create more powerful equipment – as well as upgrades to the 3D Printer and even the Forward Operating Base itself. Recipes can also be found on deployments and, presuming you extract in one piece, you can then craft those items for your Operator back at the FOB. When focused on crafting new equipment, the two key things you’ll be looking for when looting on deployments will be Resources and 3D Printer Ingredients – these are the two types of main elements to craft all items. There are four basic Resources to find during a deployment: Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, and Metals, automatically broken down from looted items, into your Backpack and Stash. 3D Printer Ingredients are rarer materials found in specific areas of Hajin and are valuable as an ingredient to make a new Item. Examples include Binding Catalyst, Biomaterials, Detonators, and Control Units, to name a few. Once you have enough of these two types of materials, you can select how many copies of an item you want to craft at once, then choose where crafted items go: send completed items directly to your Stash for later or equip them directly to your Operator to quickly prepare for the next deployment. Having this flexibility in how you want to engage the enemy during your deployment can open a variety of experiences in DMZ and can make each deployment feel like it matters, even if you come back to the FOB with zero kills to your name – at least you’ve got handful of electronics or a comms module to make it worth your time. Extraction shooters are always more engaging when every deployment has a clear purpose. That’s not going to be problem with DMZ as it will offer three ways to deploy: Story Missions, Dynamic Operations, and Free Roam. Of those, Story Missions and Dynamic Operations are two that really stand out with their defined objectives and high-tier rewards. According to the Call of Duty Blog , Story Missions will feature narrative-led deployments that you can complete and replay, though some remain locked until prerequisites are met. Each entry provides briefing intel, required objectives, and rewards – usually high-value gear and DMZ Cash – along with options for a random mission and additional milestone rewards. Dynamic Operations, meanwhile, give squads multiple goals to pursue within the DMZ. After deploying, you choose an operation and complete its objectives to earn DMZ XP, Cash, and the ability to call in a Supply Drop filled with unpredictable loot. That extra payoff adds anticipation to every successful Op while making Dynamic Operations a promising source of both Cash and XP. Persistent Operators may be DMZ’s most exciting feature because they allow Hajin to leave a lasting mark on you. You’ll begin with two Operator slots, and unlock a third as you progress through DMZ levels. Each Operator then grows stronger by surviving deployments and earning DMZ XP. Each successful exfil levels up your Operator’s Dog Tags, and this is the key to gaining Trait Points for your Operator. You can invest those points across the Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist Trait Trees, creating a meaningful choice between specialization and flexibility: with a maximum of 18 points to earn, and a choice of over 60 Trait Points to augment your Operator, you can tailor each Operator to your skills and preferred role. For example, Warfighter Traits include Combat Resistance, Quick Fix, and Viper Sense; Scout Traits include improved Thermal Padding, UAV Upgrade, and Field Crafting; while Survivalist Traits include Faster and Free Revives, increased Consumable Duration, and many more. But here’s where it gets dicey: if an Operator fails to extract and becomes MIA, you must either recover them with DMZ Cash or dismiss them. Because recovery costs rise with Trait investment, bringing back a high-level Operator becomes increasingly expensive. Recovered Operators keep their Traits but lose their gear, putting real weight behind every deployment. The chase for loot is at the heart of every extraction shooter, and DMZ makes each haul matter beyond the current deployment. Returning to base with a pack full of supplies doesn’t just feel rewarding – it improves your chances of success the next time you enter Hajin. Once you drop into a deployment, looting should be a top priority. sources.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
sources.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month. Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access , with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S. Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below. DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2 . It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it. The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone. "There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'" Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. stories.title: GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Release Build With Full Story Mode Played to the End, Ties Lucia's Clothing to Crypto Scheme
stories.summary: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to release a build of the game with the full story mode played to the end, as part of their heavily criticized crypto scheme.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Release Build With Full Story Mode Played to the End, Ties Lucia's Clothing to Crypto Scheme
sources.text: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to release a build of the game with the full story mode played to the end, as part of their heavily criticized crypto scheme. According to online reports , the Cyberleek website was updated with a warning that if its memecoin reached a market cap of $30 million, a build of GTA 6 would be released featuring the full story mode including end credits. In the alleged online warning, Cyberleek once again framed their GTA 6 leaks as a protest against the lack of a physical disc version of the game, and allegedly called on Take-Two to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue an apology. It is unclear whether Cyberleek intends to release a build of the game online, or means to release a full playthrough of GTA 6 in video form. A cryptocurrency market capitalization (market cap) is the total dollar value of all the coins or tokens of a digital asset currently in circulation. At the time of this article’s publication, Cyberleek had a market cap of $3.8 million, having spiked at $5.7 million earlier today as reports of the message hit social media. It seems unlikely that it will get anywhere near $30 million. Cyberleek also issued market cap goals tied to the clothing Lucia would wear in subsequent leaked gameplay. For example, at $2 million, Cyberleek threatened to release gameplay showing Lucia wearing a bikini. According to Cyberleek, a $4 million market cap would mean releasing gameplay with Lucia “fully naked.” However, there is significant skepticism about Cyberleek’s support of physical media, with many accusing the leaker of running a cryptocurrency scam. Fans have heavily criticized Cyberleek and anyone who spends money on their memecoin. “What a dork,” one person said. “Anyone who puts money into this deserves to lose it all.” Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Rockstar parent company Take-Two. The film issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged this week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. This week’s developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action. In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out," earning around $270,000 in the process. Every video posted by Cyberleek pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency. Such a poll is reportedly live on Cyberleek's website now , suggesting yet another leak is on the way. Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible. sources.title: GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Leak Playable Build of Grand Theft Auto VI From ‘Beginning to End’
sources.text: The notorious GTA 6 leaker known as ‘cybeleek’ has threatened to leak a playable build of Grand Theft Auto 6 from ‘beginning to end’. The threats came on the leaker’s website, which we have decided not to share as it could potentially contain malware. Whether the threats are legitimate remains to be seen, but they come after the leaker posted 25 minutes of GTA 6 gameplay , which he seemingly also modded to make Jason playable naked and a snippet of Lucia topless . According to his website, Cyberleek says he’ll release the GTA 6 build if his cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million. Cyberleek claims that the build includes the full story mode that can be “played to the end” with the end-game credits. The post also says Take-Two Interactive could avoid the leak by apologizing for not releasing a physical version of the game, and that they must also release GTA 6 physically. At the time of writing, the threats do not come with a deadline. Again, it’s unclear whether this is just one last attempt at fame before the game’s release, or whether there’s any legitimacy behind it. So far, Cyberleek has released over an hour of footage from GTA 6, but many online speculate that the leaked footage originates from an old build, rather than something more up to date. So a full playable build leak could be a bluff. Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently scheduled to release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S|X on November 19, 2026. sources.title: GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is now reportedly threatening to release a full, playable build of the game
sources.text: A GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to put out a complete, playable build of the game, start to finish. The threat was posted on CyberLeek's website after the leaker shared 25 minutes of footage from the game earlier this week. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company, has been hunting for the person behind the leaks, and has tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity. After going quiet for a bit, CyberLeek came back with a bang this week, posting new footage from Rockstar's upcoming game that even features nude scenes, including a fully naked Jason, and a topless Lucia. Eurogamer has seen the video, and it appears to be legitimate - and, as is now traditional, has CyberLeek's emblem overlaid on top of the footage. CyberLeek now reportedly says the build will go out if their cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million, and claims it can be played through to the end credits. "Here's the deal, nice and clean," the demand reads. "CyberLeek hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out — full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick." GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on 19th November.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: GTA 6 leaker threatens to upload a build with 'full story mode'
sources.text: "Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology." Cyberleek has been uploading footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 since August, most recently a 25-minute video featuring co-protagonist Jason totally nude . Given that GTA 6's November 19 release is just over a month away, on console at least, it seems natural that interest in these kinds of leaks would wane. Cyberleek has found a new way of generating hype: promising to leak a build of the game if their memecoin's marketcap goes up another $26 million or so. "Here's the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out – full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick." The other half of the deal suggests that publisher Take-Two Interactive could prevent this by releasing GTA 6 physically and apologizing, presumably for not releasing it on discs in the first place. Which will never happen, but does fit with Cyberleek's previous history of cosplay Robin Hood consumer rights complaints. We know that Cyberleek has access to a playable build since one of the previous leaks ended with the word LEEK being machinegunned into a wall to prove the point. But an early build of GTA 6 seems like the worst possible way to play it on PC, though after the Xbox streaming thing turned out to be a bust , maybe there are people who don't want to wait? Personally I'm looking forward to a slow November where I might actually get a chance to catch up on this year's other releases, like The Blood of Dawnwalker and that Hellraiser game that just came out.
